The story behind the glow

From an Egyptian oasis
to your everyday sanctuary.

In Egypt’s Western Desert, Siwa is known for its salt lakes, palms and living craft traditions. Salt is part of the oasis’s landscape and local life; its crystal forms inspire lamps with a distinctly Siwan character.

01

Born from salt water

Rock salt, or halite, forms as salty water evaporates and crystals remain. Its main component is sodium chloride: NaCl.

02

Different in daylight

Browse the photos to see pale salt surfaces and the warm glow of lit pieces. The light and thickness of the salt influence the effect.

03

A shape for your space

Spheres, hearts, flames, pyramids and crystal bowls: explore the collection and find the form that feels like you.

Simple materials. Full of character.

A carved salt body, a supporting base and an internal electric light. The pictured designs include wood or salt bases; some bowls feature coloured decorative crystals. Finishes and electrical fittings vary by model.

Keep your glow looking beautiful

  • Place on a stable, dry surface, away from water and humid rooms.
  • Unplug before cleaning. Dust gently with a dry cloth; never rinse or immerse the salt.
  • Use the correct bulb and voltage for your model, and keep the lamp out of reach of children and pets.

A few things worth knowing

Does it purify the air or offer medical benefits?

Choose it for its light, natural texture and atmosphere. Air purification, allergy relief and other therapeutic effects have not been established for salt lamps.

Which design can I order?

The gallery shows the collection’s variety. Contact Carmen to confirm current models, dimensions, electrical specifications, price and delivery before ordering.

Why keep it dry?

Salt dissolves in water and can be affected by humidity. A dry indoor setting and careful handling help protect the salt and the surface underneath.
